themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 64 THIS WEEK, a 374% increase from the 13.5-weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.91), suggesting rapid deterioration in road quality across Morris Park/Pelham Parkway that demands immediate infrastructure inspection.
evidence: 64 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.5 weekly baseline (374% increase, z-score 7.91)
Sustained spike suggests acute event (pothole season, drainage failure, or deferred maintenance coming due)
Community board has repeatedly requested streetscape improvements—suggests chronic underfunding now manifesting acutely
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: Drive routes flagged in 311 data to document specific potholes, flooding, or deterioration; interview DOT about response time
Fiscal angle: Cross-reference with DOT capital budget allocation to Morris Park vs. other districts—is this district underfunded?

themes_detail.label: Encampments and Homelessness Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints (3 THIS WEEK, 1100% above 0.2 baseline) and homeless person assistance requests (3 THIS WEEK, 2300% above 0.1 baseline) indicate an emerging street homelessness crisis in Morris Park/Pelham Parkway not previously evident in this district.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
3 homeless person assistance requests THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Both signals appeared simultaneously this week—suggests either migration into district or deteriorating conditions triggering service calls
reporting_angles: On-the-ground: Locate the 3 reported encampments; interview residents, NYPD, and DOAS about whether this reflects new migration or existing unsheltered population becoming visible
Social services angle: Is there shelter capacity at Bronx facilities? Are outreach teams reaching this district's newly visible homeless population?

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK, a 900% increase from the 0.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.2), representing the fastest-growing public safety concern in the district and warranting NYPD coordination.
evidence: 5 drug activity complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (900% increase, z-score 5.2)
Temporally correlated with encampment and homelessness spike—may indicate related public disorder cluster
No prior sustained signal in this district suggests new problem, not chronic
reporting_angles: NYPD reporting: File FOIL for recent arrests, precinct activity summaries, and whether narcotics enforcement has been deployed to Morris Park this week
Community impact: Interview residents and business owners at locations flagged in complaints about open-air drug markets, trafficking behavior, and public safety fears

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Failures
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints spiked to 7 TWO WEEKS AGO (1020% above 0.6 baseline, z-score 9.16), indicating sanitation service failures that may have triggered the subsequent street condition spike observed this week.
evidence: 7 street sweeping complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (1020% increase, z-score 9.16)
Temporally precedes the THIS WEEK street condition spike—suggests debris accumulation may have masked or worsened road deterioration
Community board budget requests include catch basin cleaning (DEP focus)—consistent with drainage/sweeping infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: DSNY operational: File FOIL for street sweeping schedules in CD 211 and actual completion dates—was service interrupted or under-resourced?
Downstream impact: Assess whether blocked catch basins from poor sweeping contributed to current street flooding/damage complaints

themes_detail.label: Elevator Maintenance Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints rose to 23 LAST WEEK, a 192% increase from the 7.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.08), affecting residents in multi-family buildings and suggesting either increased building age-related failures or contractor delays.
evidence: 23 elevator complaints last week vs. 7.9 weekly baseline (192% increase, z-score 5.08)
Concentrated signal in single category suggests cluster of buildings with maintenance issues or post-holiday service backlog
DOB data shows 174 alteration filings in 90 days—likely includes elevator modernization projects, but lag between filing and completion may explain complaints
reporting_angles: Building services: Contact DOB to identify which buildings have pending elevator permits and whether complaints correlate with delayed modernizations
Tenant impact: Interview residents in affected buildings about how long outages last and whether accessibility issues (elderly, disabled residents) are being exacerbated
